chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who gives an advance payment regarding a crop, so he takes some of his foodstuff and some remains which is not yet due/settled. So his partner presents the capital of his wealth to him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should take it, for it is permissible.' I said, 'Suppose he sells what he has taken possession of from the foodstuff, so he doubles it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if he does, then it is permissible.'

He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him about a man who gives an advance payment regarding other than a crop or a palm tree. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should name a specific amount to a specified term.'

key_terms.إِسْلَامٌ: Advance payment (pre-payment of a debt or contract value)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on taking an advance payment for crops and selling the produce to repay it in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of 'isalim' (advance payment for produce) by Imam al-Sadiq (AS), specifically addressing scenarios where the debtor settles the debt with a portion of the harvest or even sells the produce to multiply the capital, affirming the validity of such transactions. It further extends this legal framework to non-agricultural assets like palm trees, provided a specific quantity and fixed time period are agreed upon, establishing a flexible basis for Islamic commercial contracts. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for validating early forms of commodity financing and forward contracts, distinguishing them from prohibited riba (usury) by focusing on the certainty of the asset and time.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Numan, from Ibn Muskan, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who submits an advance payment regarding a farm. So he takes some of his foodstuff and there remains some (remaining), to be settled. So his companion presents the capital of his wealth to him. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should take it, for it is Permissible’. I said, ‘Supposing he were to sell what he has taken possession of, from the foodstuff, so he doubles it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he does, so it is Permissible’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who submits an advance payment regarding other than a plantation or a palm tree. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should name somthing to its named term’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali al-Nu’man from ibn Muskan from Sulayman ibn Khalid who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who makes advance payment for farms and takes a certain amount of his foodstuff and a certain amount remains. The other party offers him the remaining of his capital. He (the Imam) said, ‘He must accept it; it is lawful.’ I then said, ‘He sells his foodstuff that he has received and it doubles.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘If he does, it is lawful.’
I then asked him (the Imam) about a man who makes advance payment for what is not a farm or palm trees. He (the Imam) said, ‘He must name something for an appointed time.’”
